claims.text: A machine-learning potential such as a neural network potential can better represent the atomic configurations of an ab initio liquid in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The proposed method applies to both solid and liquid states near their high melting temperatures.
A neural network potential should be used to generate reference configurations.
Machine-learning-based reference configurations will improve representation of relevant atomic configurations.
Improved representation by the machine-learning potential will increase reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved representation by the machine-learning potential will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The intervention is applicable to equiatomic or near-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
The intervention is applicable at temperatures near or above the melting point.
Elemental or binary calculations provide supporting evidence for the proposed intervention.
The hypothesis lacks direct evidence for multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Failure of the NNP reference to significantly reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM reference would falsify the hypothesis.
